title: Focaccia
description: A classic Italian flatbread studded with olives and rosemary, baked until golden and crisp.

method.instruction: Brush a rectangular baking tin with olive oil. Combine yeast, warm water, and sugar in a large bowl. Stir to dissolve the yeast, cover, and leave in a warm place for about 10 minutes until frothy.
Add olive oil. Sift flour, milk powder, and salt into the yeast mixture. Beat with a wooden spoon until well combined, adding a little extra flour if needed to form a soft dough.
Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place dough in a large lightly oiled bowl, brush the surface with oil, cover with plastic wrap, and leave in a warm place for 1 hour or until well risen.
Punch down the dough and knead briefly. Roll out to fit the prepared tin. Cover and leave to rise for a further 20 minutes.
Using the handle of a wooden spoon, press indentations into the dough at regular intervals.
Combine olive oil and crushed garlic. Brush over the surface. Top with olives and rosemary, then sprinkle with oregano and sea salt flakes.
Cover and leave to rise for a further 30 minutes until well risen.
Bake for 20–25 minutes until golden and crisp. Cut into large squares and serve warm.

notes.title: Kneading
notes.content: Proper kneading develops the gluten structure that gives this focaccia its characteristic chewy texture. The dough should be smooth and elastic — if it tears easily, keep kneading.

notes.title: Recipe Source
notes.content: Adapted from The Essential Vegetarian Cook Book, published by Murdoch Books.
